newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Blue Square Israel Q3 EPS 0.79 shekel.
newsitem.headline: Blue Square Israel Q3 EPS 0.79 shekel.

text.p: Blue Square Israel (BSI), Israel's largest retailer, said the 31 percent rise in revenues in the third quarter came from both new outlets and increased same-store sales.
Same-store sales grew 8.9 percent for supermarkets and 8.0 percent for department and specialty stores after adjusting for inflation, the company said.

"Sales per square metre improved as we continue to apply better staff-training methods, expand the sale of private-label products and provide new and enhanced services," chief executive Yacov Gelbard said in a statement.
In addition, BSI opened four new department and speciality stores, including the first Israeli Mothercare children's store.
Third-quarter revenues were also boosted by BSI's acquisition at the end of 1995 of seven Hamashbir department stores.

BSI added another supermarket to its stable, bringing the total to 119, but department store and speciality retailing's share of total revenues grew to 24 percent in the quarter from 19 percent a year ago.
Gelbard said the company had invested 153 million shekels in the first nine months of the year in acquiring land, construction and renovations.
BSI is the parent of Tel Aviv-traded Blue Square Chain Stores Properties and Investments, which reported earnings earlier on Wednesday.
